short: ISO/IEC 27017 is ISO and IEC guidance on information security controls for cloud service providers and customers, built on ISO/IEC 27002; the current edition is ISO/IEC 27017:2026, and it is a guidance document, not a management system standard on its own.
title: ISO/IEC 27017, Information Security Controls for Cloud Services
subtitle: ISO/IEC guidance on information security controls for providing and using cloud services, built on ISO/IEC 27002
body_html:
What ISO/IEC 27017 is

ISO/IEC 27017 is guidance on information security controls for cloud services, published jointly by ISO and IEC and owned by committee ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27. The current edition is ISO/IEC 27017:2026, the second edition, published on 27 July 2026. It replaces ISO/IEC 27017:2015, which ISO now lists as withdrawn. The 2015 edition was titled a code of practice; the 2026 title drops that wording and describes the document as controls based on ISO/IEC 27002 for cloud services.

In ISO's scope description, the document gives guidance on information security controls that apply when cloud services are provided and when they are used. It builds on the control set in ISO/IEC 27002:2022 rather than standing alone.

What it covers

  • Extra guidance for relevant controls that already appear in ISO/IEC 27002:2022.
  • Additional controls, with guidance, that relate specifically to cloud services.
  • Controls and guidance addressed to both sides of the arrangement: cloud service customers and cloud service providers.
  • All cloud deployment models, including private cloud, with a note that private cloud use can need adjustments to fit relationships between an organisation's internal departments.

ISO describes it as a horizontal document: a common foundation for security in providing and using cloud services.

How a claim is made and checked

ISO's scope description presents ISO/IEC 27017 as guidance, not as a set of management system requirements. The management system requirements an organisation is certified against sit in ISO/IEC 27001, and ISO/IEC 27002 is the general control reference.

ISO/IEC 17021-1, the ISO/IEC standard for bodies that audit and certify management systems, describes management system certification as a third-party conformity assessment activity carried out by certification bodies. ISO/IEC 27006-1:2024 adds requirements for bodies that certify information security management systems and is written so that it can serve as a criteria document for accrediting those bodies.

The ISO records we read do not name a separate certification scheme for ISO/IEC 27017 on its own. In practice a 27017 claim is most likely to be meaningful when it is tied to an ISO/IEC 27001 certification whose scope and controls include the 27017 guidance. Ask the operator, or the certifying body, how the 27017 element was assessed.

What a claim does not mean

  • It is guidance on controls. A statement that an organisation "follows" or "aligns with" ISO/IEC 27017 is not evidence that anyone has audited it.
  • It does not replace ISO/IEC 27001. Without a valid 27001 certificate, a 27017 claim has no management system audit behind it.
  • A claim against the 2015 edition refers to a document ISO has withdrawn. It is not necessarily wrong, but check which edition the certificate or report names and when it was issued.
  • Any certificate has a scope, an issuing body and an expiry; the claim means only what that scope says.

ISO/IEC 27017 in data centers

The guidance is written for cloud service providers and customers. An operator that only rents space, power and cooling is not, by that alone, providing a cloud service, so a 27017 claim is most relevant where the operator also runs cloud, hosting or managed infrastructure services. When an operator publishes it, check:

  • Which service it applies to: a named cloud or managed service, a set of sites, or the whole company.
  • Whether it appears in the scope statement of an ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, and the certificate number, certifying body, accreditation body and dates.
  • Which edition is cited, 2015 or 2026.

Related standards

ISO/IEC 27017 sits on top of ISO/IEC 27001. For personal data in public cloud, see ISO/IEC 27018; for a privacy management system, ISO/IEC 27701. Cloud providers also publish CSA STAR entries. All are listed in the standards hub.
